question: GQ-004
subject: what the rights field actually says across all 106 want-list items

a_false_alarm_i_caught.my_first_reading: "72 of 106 carry a Creative Commons licence, not a public-domain claim — my filter has been matching CC-licensed works."
a_false_alarm_i_caught.the_full_string: "This work is available under the Creative Commons, Public Domain Mark"
a_false_alarm_i_caught.correction: The Public Domain Mark is a CC DESIGNATION FOR WORKS ALREADY IN THE PUBLIC DOMAIN, not a restrictive licence. Truncating the string at 44 characters cut off the words that changed its meaning. I read "Creative Commons" and inferred a licence before reading to the end of the sentence.

the_real_distribution: 105 of 106 are genuine public-domain designations of varying strength: 6 with an institutional copyright review, 72 with a CC Public Domain Mark, 25 asserting US public domain, 2 bare assertions. One — the 2025 user upload — says "Public Domain License", which is not a real designation and is the single weakest item in the list.
value_of_the_provenance_field: It works, but my binary label is too coarse. "unreviewed-or-user-supplied" lumps a CC Public Domain Mark together with free text an uploader typed. The STRING is now recorded, which is the part that matters; the classification needs more than two buckets.
